Claim 1 (Currently amended): An apparatus, comprising: an encoder (300) for encoding mode mapping information for a mapping between values of a mode index and modes available to encode at least a portion of a picture in a sequence of pictures, wherein the mode mapping information is adapted responsive to one or more actual parameters of the sequence, and wherein the encoder is configured to operate based on a predefined set of encoding rules.

Claim 7 (Currently amended): The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the adapted mode mapping information is updated after encoding one or more pictures of the sequence, and wherein the update is based on feedback from the encoding process.

Claim 9 (Currently amended): A method, comprising: encoding (740, 970) mode mapping information for a mapping between values of a mode index and modes available to encode at least a portion of a picture in a sequence of pictures, wherein the mode mapping information is adapted responsive to one or more actual parameters of the sequence, and wherein the encoding is performed using a predefined set of encoding rules.

Claim 25 (Currently amended): A method, comprising: decoding (820, 1030) mode mapping information for a mapping between values of a mode index and modes available to decode at least a portion of a picture in a sequence of pictures, wherein the mode mapping information is adapted responsive to one or more actual parameters of the sequence, and wherein the decoding is performed using a predefined set of decoding rules.

Claim 33 (Currently amended): A non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having video signal data encoded thereupon, comprising: mode mapping information for a mapping between values of a mode index and modes available to encode at least a portion of a picture in a sequence of pictures, wherein the mode mapping information is adapted responsive to one or more actual parameters of the sequence, and wherein the storage medium is configured to store instructions for performing the encoding and decoding operations.
